title: Exponential graph of a large-girth strong product requires more than ceil(3.1q) colors
statement_scope: Whole author Claim 3: let G be a finite simple graph with finite girth at least 6. Then, for sufficiently large q, χ(E_c(G⊠K_q))>c with c=ceil(3.1q). The statement retains the author's strong-product and exponential-graph notation.

difficulty_reason: Rule author-work-bearing-core-v1-20261114: H3 is borne by the actual construction, not by the paper title or claim length. At counterexample.tex lines 138-162 the proof defines the clique M={μ_{q+1},...,μ_c} by three distance regimes, uses girth at least 6 to verify adjacency, selects τ and a v-robust σ, and defines ν to force Λ(ν)=Λ(μ_τ), a contradiction; primary locator line 134.

difficulty_evidence.bearing_core: Construction of a clique M={μ_{q+1},...,μ_c} and a mapping ν that forces Λ(ν)=Λ(μ_τ), contradicting properness.

semantic_comparisons.basis: IP-set translation in arXiv:2412.17868v3 has no exponential graph, strong product G⊠K_q, clique construction, or chromatic lower bound.
Firecracker/edge-corona local antimagic coloring is a different graph family and invariant; no exponential-graph lower bound of the form χ(E_c(G⊠K_q))>ceil(3.1q).
AVD total chromatic number of a graph product is not the exponential-graph chromatic lower bound; the conclusion and constructed clique are different.
Multidimensional Ramsey product-clique conclusions concern monochromatic products, not exponential-graph colorings or a robust-class contradiction.
Kneser-graph orthogonality dimension/minrank does not overlap the exponential-graph strong-product construction.
